rationale.local_primary: 100 Gbit/s is one quarter of the fixed 400 Gbit/s outlet. During the already selected 10 us burst it permits 125000 bytes versus 491656 normal start bytes; not selected by intervention outcome.
rationale.shared_primary: The same quarter rate on the selected shared outlet, over 100 us, tests a multi-destination resource and sparse service. No additional traffic is introduced.
rationale.plane_primary: 50 Gbit/s over the fixed later 200 us covers the previously observed t90 differences. Apply separately to the two already selected same-peer planes; actual work may differ.
rationale.sustained_alternative: 4 Gbit/s over 400 us permits 200000 bytes, below the observed 966628 whole-scope bytes at 768:6. This tests sustained service, not a promise of credit exhaustion: the 6553-cell per-link/VL budget and closed-loop phase constraints remain fixed.
rationale.negative_controls: All other declared outlets, early/late periods outside each interval, peer plane, smaller workload, queue-empty periods and equal-rate natural bursts.
rationale.alternatives: arrival timing, transient allocation, busy serialization, actual failed CBFC head checks, other necessary completions, changed path choice under the same fixed routing algorithm.
rationale.no_positive_requirement: No new credit limit, endpoint delay, synchronization change or timing replay is permitted to create a positive result. Missing receiver-consumption backpressure remains uncovered.
